title: Native interop features
description: The rules every native conversion follows (docs/everyday-api.md, Native interop), as this crate carries them out.

entities.name: The caller names the intent
entities.description: A DateTime<FixedOffset> becomes an instant or a fixed-offset date-time only because the caller said which.
entities.behavior: At the JSON layer, from_fixed_offset takes an OffsetIntent (Instant or OffsetDateTime). For typed values the target type is the intent: Instant::try_from(dt) keeps only the point on the timeline, FixedOffsetDateTime::try_from(dt) keeps the wall time and the offset. Each other native type maps to exactly one kind of UTV value.
entities.outcome: No conversion picks a meaning for the caller, and the shared code intent-required never arises: a call without an intent doesn't compile.
constraints: FixedOffsetDateTime::try_from refuses chrono offsets beyond ±18:00 (invalid, offset-out-of-range), which chrono itself allows.
NaiveDateTime becomes an unzoned date-time; it is never read as local time or as UTC.

entities.name: No host-local values
entities.description: A chrono DateTime<Local> is refused, never interpreted with the machine's zone.
entities.behavior: from_local answers unsupported with diagnostic local-zone for every value, and its message points to from_fixed_offset or from_utc. No typed value has a From or TryFrom for DateTime<Local>.
entities.outcome: A result never depends on the time zone of the machine it ran on.
constraints: The caller converts a local reading with an explicit intent first, for example dt.fixed_offset() and from_fixed_offset(.., OffsetIntent::Instant).

entities.name: Lossy conversions back to native are refused
entities.description: Converting a UTV value to a native type that can't hold it exactly gives an error naming the loss, never an approximation.
entities.behavior: The to_* functions return Err(UtvResult) with status unsupported, and the TryFrom impls Err(Diagnostics), when the value is outside the native range (out-of-native-range), finer than a nanosecond or than the platform's SystemTime (precision-loss), or has a zone or offset the native type would drop (zone-dropped). Coming in, chrono's leap-second representation is refused with leap-second.
entities.outcome: A native value that comes back from UTV is the value UTV held.
constraints: chrono's dates reach about ±262 000 years; UTV's go to the i128 range.
SystemTime is checked by a round trip, so a platform with a coarser clock than nanoseconds refuses what it can't hold.
To NaiveTime a time without a second gets second 0 (From<CivilTime> for NaiveTime), which loses no value, only the written form.
The info code offset-not-known never arises: there is no conversion from an instant to a native type that needs an offset.

entities.name: "Now" is an input
entities.description: The library never reads the clock; the caller passes the reading in.
entities.behavior: from_system_time and Instant::from_system_time take a SystemTime the caller read (SystemTime::now(), or any fixed value in a test) and keep it exactly, before or after the epoch.
entities.outcome: The dependency on the host clock is visible in the caller's code, and a test can fix "now".
constraints: Nothing in src/ calls ::now(); tests/purity.rs searches the sources for it.
